meta.title: Who Owns What: TPS, Developer, Providers

views.label: What TPS owns
views.note: Everything that matters is in TPS's name. Like owning the land and paying for materials.

views.label: The developer's role
views.note: The builder: works inside TPS's accounts with access TPS can remove at any time.

views.label: Who gets paid
views.note: Provider fees go straight to providers; the developer charges only for maintenance and new work.

components.label: TPS
components.explanation: House analogy: TPS owns the land and pays for materials and utilities. Every account, the domain, the data and the billing sit in TPS's name, so nothing has to be handed over if the developer changes.

components.label: Domain name
components.explanation: The website address. Registered and renewed by TPS; renewal cost is not included in the hosting estimate.

components.label: Provider accounts
components.explanation: TPS creates and owns the provider organizations as administrator, then invites the developer with a role that gives only the access the work needs.

components.label: Business data
components.explanation: Production data belongs to TPS wherever it is stored: media in R2, enquiries in Zoho, bookings in SimplyBook, and any optional database.

components.label: Billing
components.explanation: Provider subscriptions and usage are billed to TPS's own payment method, so TPS sees every provider invoice directly.

components.label: Developer
components.explanation: Designs, configures and deploys the website, and assists with operations within the agreed maintenance scope. New features are quoted separately. The developer does not resell hosting; that would need a separate agreement covering support and liability.

components.label: Providers
components.explanation: Operate the underlying servers, networks and storage, like utility companies supplying power and water.
